summary: A white square tower at the southern tip of the Baccaro peninsula, built in 1934 after a fire; the first light there was lit in 1851.

lens.note: The sources read do not describe the lens in the 1934 tower. The 1903 change used apparatus from Cape Sable light (Department report).

structures.type: square tapering wooden tower with red lantern (Preservation Society); square tapered profile with red octagonal lantern (register)
structures.note: Built after the fire of January 1934. Lighthouse Directory gives 13.5 m; the Coast Guard list gives 14.0 m.

structures.type: square tower attached to a square dwelling, painted with black circles on three faces (daymark)
structures.note: Began 1850 (Preservation Society; register); lit 16 January 1851; destroyed by fire January 1934.

staffing.note: Keeper retired and station de-staffed 1984 (Lighthouse Friends). Preservation Society: automated by 1986.

access.note: Gravel road off NS 309 south of Clyde River; parking provided. Grounds open, tower closed (Lighthouse Friends; Lighthouse Directory). Maintained by the Keepers of the Baccaro Light (Preservation Society).

facts.heritage: Federal Heritage Building, DFRP 02293 (Parks Canada register)

events.note: Earlier square tower and dwelling begun in 1850 (Preservation Society 'Began: 1850'; register)
Lit 16 January 1851, with James S. Smith as keeper (Lighthouse Friends; Preservation Society 'Date Lit')
Revolving white changed to fixed red, to the dissatisfaction of many mariners (Lighthouse Friends)
English quick flashing light ordered to replace the fixed red light complained of (Department report, 1901)
Hand fog horns supplied to Baccaro and other Nova Scotia stations to answer ships' fog signals (Department report, 1901 Nova Scotia notes)
11 July 1903: fixed red changed to revolving white, 30-second interval, using apparatus from Cape Sable light (Department report, 1903)
Lighthouse destroyed by fire on 16 January 1934; keeper Herbert Ross and his family fled the dwelling (Lighthouse Friends; register; Lighthouse Directory)
Present square tapered tower built as replacement later in 1934; temporary light from a pole in the interval (Lighthouse Friends; register; Preservation Society)
One keeper's dwelling moved to Seal Point (Lighthouse Directory 1984; Lighthouse Friends gives no year)
Keeper Brenton Reynolds retired; station de-staffed (Lighthouse Friends)
Other keeper's dwelling torn down (Lighthouse Friends)
Automated by 1986 (Preservation Society). Lighthouse Friends says de-staffed 1984.
Fog alarm discontinued; a citizen started a Facebook page to seek help reactivating the foghorn (Lighthouse Friends)
Keepers of the Baccaro Light formed as a non-profit to preserve the lighthouse and grounds (Lighthouse Friends; Lighthouse Directory)
Repaired and painted with a $10,000 grant from the Municipality of Barrington and $3,344 from the National Trust of Canada (Lighthouse Friends)
Lantern room restored in the fall with the Coast Guard's help (Lighthouse Friends; Lighthouse Directory)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 1850 for the start of the first tower (Preservation Society 'Began'; register) and 16 January 1851 for when it was lit (Lighthouse Friends; Preservation Society; the record's first_lit). Both are kept: built 1850, first lit 1851. The Lighthouse Directory gives 1851 as the station year and 1934 for the tower, and a novascotiavacation.ca page (not used) gives 1852 for the hauling of materials.
The Lighthouse Directory gives 13.5 m for the 1934 tower; the Coast Guard list gives 14.0 m, which matches the record and is used here.
Lighthouse Friends says the station was de-staffed when Reynolds retired in 1984; the Preservation Society says it was automated by 1986. Both are recorded.

The Coast Guard list gives a focal height of 15 m (the record value); the Lighthouse Directory gives a focal plane of 16 m (52 ft); the Preservation Society gives a light height of 52 ft (about 15.8 m). The story states the Coast Guard and Directory figures.

notes_for_editor: Keeper roster is Lighthouse Friends' list (facts only). The 1905 keepers' list entry for Fisher (scan 343, printed 262) was removed from the story: its name and station sit in separate OCR blocks, and the page image could not be viewed (the built-in browser refused archive.org). Fisher's 1893-1907 stint now rests on Lighthouse Friends alone; the checker should read scan 343 before any 1905 claim is restored. The 1910 table pairing 'Baccaro' with 'Wm. L. Smith' (scan 256, printed 254) sits on one OCR line; its page image was not viewed either. The 1901 hand fog horn passage is on scan 74, printed page 59, per the report's own index (scan 6: 'Baccaro-Hand fog-horns supplied 59'). Height: Lighthouse Directory 13.5 m and focal plane 16 m; Coast Guard 14.0 m and focal height 15 m; both are now stated in the story. Staffing: 1984 de-staffing (Lighthouse Friends) vs automated by 1986 (Preservation Society). The record's fog signal 'horn' is not checked against a Department source for the 1934 tower; the 2014 fog alarm discontinuance (Lighthouse Friends) is a later status change the record does not carry. The Preservation Society's lens and characteristic entries for 1883, 1922 and 1941 were not used because no Department source for those years was read to check them. 1850 (register; Preservation Society) and 1851 (Lighthouse Friends; Preservation Society date lit; record) are both used. The 1852 materials date on novascotiavacation.ca was not used (a tourism page). Keepers Reynolds (retired 1984), Nickerson, Blache and Ross are named in their public role; the one personal detail (the bicycle ride from Port La Tour) is Lighthouse Friends' and is kept as a single sourced sentence.
